pr_title: EditorHelpBit: Fix content height fit and RTL theme propagation
pr_body:
This reverts #51619 and fixes the issue properly, as well as enabling
`fit_content_height` which is necessary following #57304.

- Fixes #57174.

Also adds placeholder for property and signal tooltips with no description,
factoring the code while at it.

Thanks @bruvzg for the hints.

---

Before:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/152170241-34c1a4e7-7f1c-4115-bae2-ca652e60ba71.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/152169830-dcc0cc43-20ea-41bd-8173-9497e3500cfd.png)

After:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/152170051-f484c053-66d2-45c2-abbf-c4c97a4893c5.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/152170131-869a7a28-7a93-4573-a562-e1a5031685cb.png)
(Was meant to be italics but we don't set an italics font for the `EditorHelp` it seems.)
pr_comments: Actually that's not enough, I _also_ need to revert #51619 for it to work.
I guess with #51619 popup window is checking for RTL size before text is set (so it's size of an empty label), and I do not think there's any code that's recalculating window size after its creation.

Thanks, it seems to work well!

While at it I did some cleanup and tweaks to the `EditorInspector` code that creates the tooltips.

BTW I noticed another unexpected behavior with property tooltips:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/152170657-19da1b24-17d7-47bb-8c1e-6783eeab5a84.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/152170589-18a67a65-82a4-437a-af9b-d5244204ec90.png)

For `rect_size` there seems to be an extra line / the tooltip height doesn't fit the content exactly. I thought it might be a stray `\n` but it doesn't seem to be the case:
```
(gdb) print property_name
$1 = {_cowdata = {_ptr = 0x184977b0 U"rect_size"}}
(gdb) print property_doc
$2 = {_cowdata = {_ptr = 0x1992b180 U"The size of the node's bounding rectangle, in pixels. [Container] nodes update this property automatically."}}
```

Might be because it's so close to wrapping that the calculations somehow make the height bigger than needed?

Also, notice that the same pattern from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/51619 used at:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c8ee8082f49f4051d7143e24961c45c56910997a/editor/connections_dialog.cpp#L549

> Also, notice that the same pattern from #51619 used at:
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c8ee8082f49f4051d7143e24961c45c56910997a/editor/connections_dialog.cpp#L549

Ah good call, this was indeed buggy too:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/152187815-efc501cf-7acf-400a-bc41-ff4c41fffcb3.png)

I'll fix it up.

Fixed up the `ConnectionsDialog` which indeed had the same problem for the same reason.

I checked other uses of `EditorHelpBit` and then didn't seem to defer updates.

> BTW I noticed another unexpected behavior with property tooltips At least final RTL min. size and content size seems to be correct, so it's not related to line breaks, not sure why window is bigger. Probably some intermediate state during `_add_text_to_rt` which has an unclosed tag is bigger, and it did not shrink back. Adding `rich_text->set_size(Size2(0, 0));` after `_add_text_to_rt` in the notifications should shrink it to min. size and fix the issue.

> At least final RTL min. size and content size seems to be correct, so it's not related to line breaks, not sure why window is bigger. Probably some intermediate state during `_add_text_to_rt` which has an unclosed tag is bigger, and it did not shrink back.

That makes sense, the size might be calculated based on that string with `[Container]` instead of `Container` (and thus possibly not properly taking into account the different font? Might be something to keep in mind if we see future issues around this).

> Adding `rich_text->set_size(Size2(0, 0));` after `_add_text_to_rt` in the notifications should shrink it to min. size and fix the issue.

I've added this for now (using the new `reset_size()` which is nicer :)) as it doesn't cost much.

> Might be something to keep in mind if we see future issues around this).

Might be font, or it's `p_rt->add_text("[");` which is displayed as a visible `[` char until tag is finished.
I guess adding some sort of bulk update mode to prevent recalculation after every single portion of text added might be worth it.

issue_context.title: Tooltip boxes not expanding correctly to show multiple lines in editor.
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.alpha1.official

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Property tooltip boxes often cut through a line of text:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61291296/150894762-895a44e8-71ec-485a-ba28-92cba6a8299b.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61291296/150894803-d3fa9254-7c28-4e2f-9124-81afa9d94a51.png)

The tooltip's size is not consitent, nor is the 'cut hieght':

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61291296/150894946-fe92a872-32a1-45bc-9343-0112a91ed0b7.png)

It looks like only single-line tooltips display properly:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61291296/150895258-e581be8d-6ecc-44ce-a33b-947e9d385c30.png)

Altering Windows' app scaling (this settings option:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61291296/150896899-7255f90b-d3bb-472a-be93-5e55b5e1b89a.png)) didn't change the behaviour.

### Steps to reproduce

Open the editor and mouseover a property in the inspector.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments: Hmm, I think you can use mouse scrolling now (252ec22ff9fc2befd6b120fd40b0e008137a0392) to see the full content of the tooltip.
@Chaosus: Not everyone has a mouse (I don't, I use a trackpad)

@Zireael07 It doesn't work with a trackpad?
![test](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3036176/151655238-6cbf9479-3d28-4744-9fa5-4c40dce57577.gif)
It should be possible to calculate the popup size to fit the contents, and maybe just have a max size for very long descriptions to give them a scrollbar.
I tested some pre-alpha builds, the size issue started between 4.0-dev.20210811 (7188cb601) and 4.0-dev.20210820 (75697c0df): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/7188cb601...75697c0df

Bisected, it's a regression from #51619. Proves that going for a hack is always going to bite us back :)
CC @Chaosus @godotengine/gui-nodes

@akien-mga Are you sure? - I reverted it and see no difference - 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3036176/152157430-908e3c0b-d36f-4f57-96ab-7402b45af02f.png)

Can't test it right now, but seems like RTL in the `EditorHelpBit` do not have `fit_content_height` set, so it's not calculating min. height, which was broken before `#57304` and was updating only after multiple redraws. This might what's causing this be an issue.

That was the result of the bisect yes, so I'm pretty sure that #51619 caused the regression. But indeed reverting it does not fix the issue in current `master`, probably because the tooltip now has a scrollbar (which was not the case just a couple of weeks ago in 4.0 alpha 1). I assume the scrollbar was added via #57304.
Adding `set_fit_content_height(true)` does seem to solve the issue (without reverting #51619, which reintroduces the color issue).

> Adding `set_fit_content_height(true)` does seem to solve the issue (without reverting #51619, which reintroduces the color issue).

I spoke too fast. With only #57547 the bug is still reproducible. I need both to revert #51619 and enable `set_fit_content_height` to solve it.

review_comments: This was commented out in `EditorProperty`'s implementation, and I couldn't notice a difference between category (Node names) and property tooltips, so I removed it.

Removed this because it was causing tooltips with no description to look like they were still adding empty lines:
![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/152169830-dcc0cc43-20ea-41bd-8173-9497e3500cfd.png)

Now the height always fits the content. If there's no content, it falls back to a default tooltip.

I changed my mind and added it back, since it would cause this on wrongly initialized entries:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/57547#issuecomment-1028078230
